title: Feed compact entry tints + Jeffershizzle browse return
content:
Tonight's pass stayed intentionally small and practical. Feed's manual-entry editor was tightened into a more compact authoring surface, while Jeffershizzle's browse-view image flow was corrected so archive browsing and spiderweb wandering stay meaningfully separate.

What changed:

  • Feed composer compacted: manual entries now keep Title and Publish Date on the same row instead of stacking the date above everything else.
  • Compact tint popup: the earlier full-width tint section was replaced by a small popup color chooser beside Publish Date, with 16 preset colors and hover labels.
  • Tint persistence: Feed now stores tint choices in MySQL through a new tint_color field, so create/edit/reload/live display all stay in sync.
  • Jeffershizzle browse correction: when a viewer comes from #/browse, clicking an image enlarges it as expected, and clicking the enlarged image now returns them cleanly to browse instead of pushing them into the original spiderweb link path.

The important design decision here was restraint. The tint feature is useful, but it should feel like a small editorial choice rather than a control panel. And on Jeffershizzle, browse mode needed to stay browse mode: enlargement is good, but the archive path should not quietly become the spiderweb path unless the viewer actually chose that experience.
